name.description: Option name. Returned as `choice` and used as the key in `probabilities`. Sent to the model.
name.title: Name

description.description: What this option covers. Omit when the name is clear on its own. An object can carry a rubric, e.g. {what, not_for, examples}, or a taxonomy subtree.
description.title: Description

ChoiceQuestion.description: Which of these options? For a fixed set of unordered options.

id.description: Your key for this question; the answer comes back under it. Not sent to the model.
id.title: Id

instructions.description: What the model should decide, written as a complete question. Reference parts of a structured state by path in backticks, e.g. `ticket.messages[0].text`. An object can hold the question in one field and data it refers to in others.
instructions.title: Instructions

options.description: The answer options (2 to 255). Give the full list, and add an `other` option when the list might not cover every input.
options.title: Options

ChoiceQuestion.title: ChoiceQuestion

NoulQuestion.description: Is this true? For a clean yes/no where the probability itself is the signal.

id.description: Your key for this question; the answer comes back under it. Not sent to the model.
id.title: Id

instructions.description: The yes/no question, or a statement to judge. Make the boundary between yes and no unambiguous. Reference parts of a structured state by path in backticks.
instructions.title: Instructions

criteria.description: Optional. Pins down a subtle yes/no boundary.

NoulQuestion.title: NoulQuestion

ScoreQuestion.description: Which level? For a position on a spectrum you can describe.

id.description: Your key for this question; the answer comes back under it. Not sent to the model.
id.title: Id

instructions.description: What the model should rate, written as a complete question. Reference parts of a structured state by path in backticks.
instructions.title: Instructions

levels.description: Ordered level descriptions, low end to high end (2 to 10). A level's number is its index, starting at 0. Describe situations, not degrees: each level is judged on its own and the model never sees its number or its neighbours.
levels.title: Levels

ScoreQuestion.title: ScoreQuestion

state.description: The content to evaluate: a string, or a JSON object / array of related context (messages, records, a policy). Text only. Every question sees the same state. Send only what the questions need; unrelated detail costs accuracy.
examples: Our API started returning 500 errors 20 minutes ago and we can't process any customer orders.
state.title: State

choices.description: Choice questions: pick one option from a set.
choices.title: Choices

scores.description: Score questions: place the state on ordered levels.
scores.title: Scores

nouls.description: Noul questions: probability that the answer is yes.
nouls.title: Nouls

model.description: Model name or alias: `jev-latest`, `jev-preview`, or a pinned version such as `jev-1.13.0`. Pin a version if you tuned thresholds against it.
model.title: Model
